result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put the recipe first on phones, cap the layout on ultrawide screens and give CSS a developer can build from. B places its em-based breakpoints where another column fits, not at named devices, and checks the fit with arithmetic, such as flagging that the recipe column is only about 540px at 1200px. Its spec is also tighter. A covers more tiers and adds useful extras such as print styles and ad placement, but its breakpoints are tied to devices, and it is longer and somewhat more like general advice. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers put the recipe first on phones, set phone padding, and cap the width on very large screens while keeping a readable line length. A ties each breakpoint to the point where another column fits, uses em units, and gives a compact CSS grid sketch the developer can build from directly. B is more detailed about content order and components, but it bases its breakpoints on named device classes, and its longer CSS sketch is less complete.
